title: Designing a CI Pipeline knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Designing a CI Pipeline?
options: A CI pipeline should run relevant fast checks, tests, and build steps on change events and produce clear, required pass/fail checks.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: A CI pipeline should run relevant fast checks, tests, and build steps on change events and produce clear, required pass/fail checks.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of designing a ci pipeline: A CI pipeline should run relevant fast checks, tests, and build steps on change events and produce clear, required pass/fail checks. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to designing a ci pipeline?
options: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: A CI pipeline should run relevant fast checks, tests, and build steps on change events and produce clear, required pass/fail checks. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
